text: Brennick University researchers behind the Ostrava Lake sediment study said Monday that the samples were taken from the lake’s eastern basin over a six-week period and analyzed at the school’s coastal geology lab. The team found unusually high mineral layering consistent with long-term runoff from nearby farmland, according to a summary released by the university. Harborview environmental officer Lena Voss said the findings help explain recent water-quality changes. “This gives us a much clearer picture of what has been building up in the lake for years,” Voss said. The study, led by Dr. Tomas Reid, used core samples collected in March and April and is expected to be published next month.
